```

```

title: Powershell getVolumes() bug
description:
There seems to be a bug in the powershell command for getting the drives.
Write-Output does not write an output for VolumeLabel if the drives [IsReady](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.driveinfo.isready?view=net-6.0#system-io-driveinfo-isready) flag is set to "False" 0  (e.g. a Network drive is not connected), then the matrix gets shifted by one and the names don't match anymore.

Possible fix:
```
volumes.info <- system2("powershell",shQuote('[System.IO.DriveInfo]::GetDrives() | Where-Object {$_.IsReady -eq 1} | foreach {$_.Name+"`n"+$_.VolumeLabel}'), stdout = TRUE)
if(length(volumes.info) == 0) return(NULL)
mat <- matrix(volumes.info, ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
```
 * checks for IsReady flag

title: Warnings for the lengths in conditions when choosing files and folders
description:
Hi and thank you for the wonderful package.

Today I updated to the latest R version (4.2.0). The [package I have](https://cran.r-project.org/package=RALSA) uses `shinyFiles` to choose input and output files and folders. Until the update to R 4.2.0 it all worked fantastic. After the update it still works, but warning messages started appearing in the console when I click on a `shinyFiles` button and choose files and folders in the dialog windows, such as:

`Warning in is.null(tree) || is.na(tree) :`
`  'length(x) = 8 > 1' in coercion to 'logical(1)'`

`Warning in is.null(files$dir) || is.na(files$dir) :`
`  'length(x) = 5 > 1' in coercion to 'logical(1)'`

`Warning in is.null(dir) || is.na(dir) :`
`  'length(x) = 2 > 1' in coercion to 'logical(1)'`

The actual numbers for the `length(x) = X` part differ for different `shinyFiles` buttons in the application, I assume it is also related with the lengths of the paths to files and folders. I managed to track the code quoted in the warnings to the following files in the `shinyFiles` package:

- `is.null(tree) || is.na(tree)` - [dirchoose.R](https://github.com/thomasp85/shinyFiles/blob/master/R/dirchoose.R), line 219
- `is.null(files$dir) || is.na(files$dir)` - [dirchoose.R](https://github.com/thomasp85/shinyFiles/blob/master/R/dirchoose.R), line 229
- `is.null(dir) || is.na(dir)` - [filesave.R](https://github.com/thomasp85/shinyFiles/blob/master/R/filesave.R), line 56

I am not sure what would be the reason for this, but I suppose it is related with one of the [latest changes in R (v4.2.0)](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/NEWS.html):
"Calling && or || with either argument of length greater than one now gives a warning (which it is intended will become an error)."

What really bothers me is the last part, "which it is intended will become an error".

Thank you in advance for your response.

title: Have MyDocuments and Desktop in getvolumes (with solution)
description:
Right now to have MyDocuments and Desktop as volumes on Windows machines I am using this.

(Note that this depends on powershell being available)

```r
  myVolumes <- function() {
    if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
      extra_volumes <- c(Desktop = system2("powershell", "[Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop')", stdout = TRUE),
                         MyDocuments = system2("powershell", "[Environment]::GetFolderPath('MyDocuments')", stdout = TRUE),
                         UserProfile = system2("powershell", 'echo $env:USERPROFILE', stdout = TRUE))
    } else {
      extra_volumes <- c()
    }
    c(extra_volumes, shinyFiles::getVolumes()())
  }
```
And then
```r
  shinyFileChoose(input, 'whatever', roots = mygetVolumes)
```

Maybe this would be a nice addition to `getVolumes`.

Currently `getVolumes` returns a function that is called very often, to see if there are updates on any volume (new USB attached, etc). This has a strong performance penalty on Windows.

To address the performance penalty it would be useful to have a refresh button next to the volume selection menu so getVolumes is only called every once in a while.

As a workaround, if you don't care about "new attached USB drives" you can use:


```r
  list_of_volumes <- mygetVolumes()
  shinyFileChoose(input, 'whatever', roots = list_of_volumes)
```
